definition: Situation, complication, question, answer, then pillars of evidence, then recommendation and appendix. Titles alone must carry the argument.
examples: 20-60 slides, 30-60 minutes or read as a document
title -> exec summary -> situation -> complication -> question/agenda -> per pillar (section header + 3-6 action-title evidence slides) -> recommendation/next steps -> appendix

definition: The Sequoia ten-slide company narrative, optionally extended with traction, go-to-market and the ask.
examples: title -> company purpose -> problem -> solution -> why now -> market size -> competition -> product -> business model -> team -> financials

definition: Ten slides, twenty minutes, nothing below 30pt.
examples: title -> problem -> value proposition -> underlying magic -> business model -> go-to-market -> competition -> team -> financials -> status and use of funds

definition: A pitch told in three acts: setup, proof of product, proof of business.
examples: act 1 cover, traction teaser, problem, market -> act 2 solution, product, how it works, audience, case study, business model, roadmap -> act 3 traction, unit economics, go-to-market, TAM, competition, secret sauce, team, financials, ask

definition: Alternating "what is" and "what could be" around a call to adventure, ending in a call to action and new bliss.
examples: title -> what is -> call to adventure -> 3-5 what is / what could be pairs -> call to action -> new bliss

definition: Hook, objectives, recall, concept, worked example, guided case, practice, feedback, check, recap.
examples: 10-20 slides per module, 1 slide per 1-2 minutes

definition: Overall status, dimension RAG table, milestones, accomplishments, upcoming, risks, decisions needed.
examples: 4-6 slides, under 30 seconds of executive scan per slide
at most 5-7 workstreams in the RAG table; 2-4 items per accomplishment, upcoming and risk block

definition: Welcome, objectives, timed agenda, icebreaker, then framing / activity / timer / debrief blocks, ending in takeaways and next steps.
examples: 15-30 slides per 2 hours; an activity every 15-20 minutes; at most 3 framing slides per block

definition: An unpresented read-deck: cover, one-page executive summary, contents, then dense topic pages, recommendations and appendix.
examples: 100 words per page target, 250 maximum; 2-4 dense text and figure pages per topic

definition: One word, phrase or image per slide, synchronised to speech; no bullets.
